findings.headline: EGP/USD ~51.0 on 09-Sep-2026 (mid-market 1 EGP = USD 0.0196); the pound is down 6.41% against the dollar year-to-date in 2026 and traded 0.01954-0.02001 in the week to 02-Sep-2026
findings.source_name: Wise and poundsterlinglive USD-EGP daily mid-market series
findings.detail: FX quotes are PRIMARY_MARKET_DATA, a sanctioned source class. The Central Bank of Egypt's own page was WAF-blocked, see the primary-access log.
findings.model_impact: Sets the translation rate for the ~67-70% of revenue that is international and for the ~99%-foreign-currency debt stack (F27). A -6.4% YTD move is an EGP revenue TAILWIND and a finance-cost and translation-reserve headwind at the same time; both legs must run off the same rate path, not two.

findings.headline: Polypropylene repriced sharply in 1Q-2026 on the US-Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz disruption: German PP rose from ~USD 1,063/MT in Jan-2026 to ~USD 1,346/MT in Mar-2026 (+26.6%); US PP from ~USD 1,027/MT to ~USD 1,351/MT (+31.5%); European propylene contract prices rose ~7% with a step change between March and April 2026
findings.source_name: Procurement Resource polypropylene price-trend series; ChemAnalyst; PlasticsToday; Argus reporting of LyondellBasell on Iran-war polymer repricing
findings.detail: Corroborates the company's OWN polypropylene series (F21), which rose from EGP 948 in 1Q-2026 to EGP 1,246 in 2Q-2026, +31% q/q — the same shock in the company's own units. This is the single largest input: polypropylene/nylon is 51% of raw materials and raw materials are ~50% of COGS, so PP is roughly a quarter of cost of sales.
findings.model_impact: Drives the raw-material cost-per-square-metre leg of the bottom-up COGS build. Gross margin is the OUTPUT of that build, never an input.

findings.headline: Global carpet and rug market ~USD 60.1bn in 2025 heading to ~USD 64.7bn in 2026; the top five players hold 17.6% between them. Mohawk Industries' 2Q-2026 net sales were USD 3.0bn, +6.8% reported and +5.0% adjusted, with management stating the home resale market is near multi-decade lows and new home construction remains soft, commercial outperforming residential
findings.source_name: Grand View Research carpet and rug market sizing; Mohawk Industries 2Q-2026 results release and earnings call
findings.detail: ORWE's own 4Q-2025 deck claims a 10% global woven market share and presence in 118+ countries, so world demand is not background for this issuer — it is roughly two thirds of the revenue base.
findings.model_impact: Caps international volume growth. The explicit window cannot assume a Western residential recovery that the largest listed competitor says has not started.

findings.headline: The US tariff regime on Egyptian carpets reset twice inside the historical window: the QIZ/GSP duty-free route for Egyptian carpets and textile floor coverings was overridden by a blanket 10% ad-valorem tariff in April 2025; the IEEPA reciprocal tariffs were struck down by the US Supreme Court on 20-Feb-2026 and replaced by a 10% Section 122 global surcharge effective 24-Feb-2026, leaving Egypt at 10%
findings.source_name: USAFacts average US tariff rate by country (Egypt); tariffcheck.org Egypt guide; Passport Global 2026 tariff-rate compilation
findings.detail: The Americas were 34% of 2Q-2026 revenue (F19) and America grew 29% YoY in that quarter despite the surcharge. Mohawk's 2Q-2026 numbers carry tariff REFUNDS, guided at ~USD 0.12 per share into 3Q-2026 — the same legal event seen from the importer's side.
findings.model_impact: A named, dated 10% duty wedge on the single largest export destination. Model as an explicit price and margin term on the Americas leg, dual-framed with and without, never smoothed into an ASP glide.

findings.category: sovereign macro (inflation, policy rate, FX/deval risk)
findings.headline: The CBE held the overnight deposit rate at 19.00% and the lending rate at 20.00% on 20-Aug-2026, a fourth consecutive hold. Headline inflation rose to 14.9% in Jul-2026 (core 14.7%) from 14.3% in Jun-2026, though monthly headline and core both printed 0.0% in July. The CBE's stated target remains 7% +/-2pp on average in Q4-2026, with single digits expected in H2-2027
findings.source_name: Bloomberg and Central Banking reporting of the CBE Monetary Policy Committee decision of 20-Aug-2026
findings.detail: PROVENANCE EXCEPTION, STATED: cbe.org.eg returned an F5 'Request Rejected' WAF page, support ID da44b8f3-d541-4d41-af65-ffc44ffcdaa2, so the regulator's own page could not be read. This is a Country-ring regulator figure, not an ORWE-reported figure. NOTE the 19-20% EGP policy rate is NOT this issuer's cost of debt — see F27, an implied ~7.0% on a 99%-foreign-currency stack.
findings.model_impact: Anchors the explicit-window EGP risk-free rate and the terminal build, which is norm-built off the CBE's own 7% target rather than a historical average. Does NOT set Kd: that leg is dollar-linked.

findings.headline: Egypt's Export Burden Rebate Program for FY2025/26 was doubled to EGP 45bn (EGP 38bn to priority sectors including textiles and home furnishings, EGP 7bn flexible reserve); the FY2026/27 budget allocates EGP 48bn. The ~EGP 60bn of pre-July-2024 arrears is being settled half in cash over four years and half by set-off against exporters' obligations to state entities, with EGP 12.6bn (50% of the cash portion) already paid to ~2,500 companies inside one fiscal year
findings.source_name: Egyptian Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade programme announcements, reported via Daily News Egypt, Business Today Egypt, Amwal Al Ghad and the State Information Service
findings.detail: DRIVER UNLOCK. This is the mechanism behind ORWE's export-rebate income, and the company's own numbers name the same two channels: 2Q-2026 EGP 452m collected 'including EGP 150m from backlog claims settled through government fee offsets and cash collections'. F17 shows the rebate IS the audited 'Other revenues' line, to the pound.
findings.model_impact: Converts export-rebate income from a residual into a bottom-up build: a current-programme accrual on export value plus a scheduled run-off of the named EGP 180m remaining backlog. Sensitise the programme's continuation separately — 1H-2026 rebates were 32% of net profit.

findings.headline: Three of the six consolidated subsidiaries — Oriental Weavers International, Oriental Weavers Textile and New Mac — are established under Investment Guarantee and Incentives Law No. 8 of 1997 in a PRIVATE FREE ZONE and are, per their tax cards, exempt from corporate tax for the lifetime of the company. Egypt's headline corporate rate is 22.5%
findings.source_name: ORWE FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements, note 33 'Tax position', sub-notes 33-2, 33-3 and 33-5 (read off the rendered pixels, printed pages 28-29)
findings.model_impact: Effective tax is a BOTTOM-UP driver off the free-zone mix, not a 22.5% statutory plug. A build that applies 22.5% understates net profit by roughly ten percentage points of pre-tax income.

findings.category: fiscal / political events with sector read-through
findings.headline: Egypt is targeting USD 11.5bn of annual textile export revenue by 2030 against USD 2.8bn earned in 2024, and is pulling in foreign capacity: Turkish group Boni's USD 100m integrated factory in 10th of Ramadan City, Chinese EVERFAR Textile Egypt USD 130m, Changzhou Kingcason USD 24.5m and Shanghai Honour Home Textile. Around 1,700 Turkish businesses have invested over USD 3bn in Egypt with ~200 factories in textiles, garments and chemicals concentrated in 10th of Ramadan, Sadat City and the Suez Canal Economic Zone
findings.source_name: Ecofin Agency; Kohan Textile Journal; EnterpriseAM Egypt; AmCham Egypt textile and ready-made-garments study
findings.detail: ORWE's own plants are in 10th of Ramadan City, the same cluster. The named investments are garments and home textiles rather than machine-woven carpet lines — see the dated negative search F42.
findings.model_impact: Two-sided. Supports the continuation of the export-rebate programme (F14) that carries a third of 1H-2026 net profit, and raises competition for skilled labour in the same industrial zone, which is the mechanism behind the +21% to +27% YoY wage inflation the company reports (F22).

findings.headline: ORWE's disclosed nameplate is 150m sqm a year across 26 production facilities on two continents: woven 79m sqm, tufted 48.1m sqm, non-woven 23m sqm (79 + 48.1 + 23 = 150.1, which foots to the stated 150m). Group sales volume was 138.7m sqm in FY2021, 121.8m in FY2022, 112.7m in FY2023, 113.8m in FY2024 and 111.2m in FY2025
findings.source_name: ORWE FY2022 Investor Presentation, 'Well-Invested Production Facilities' pages 15-17; volumes from the FY2024 earnings release volume tables and the 4Q-2025 investor presentation quarterly volume chart
findings.detail: Implied utilisation: FY2021 92%, FY2022 81%, FY2023 75%, FY2024 76%, FY2025 74%. The capacity figure is a FY2022-vintage disclosure and no later nameplate has been published — see the negative search F42. The 4Q-2025 non-woven capacity addition management refers to is not quantified anywhere.
findings.model_impact: DRIVER UNLOCK: caps the volume driver and makes the volume build a utilisation path against a named nameplate rather than a growth rate. [R-ASSET-01] — the asset base's vintage is FY2022, older than this sweep's information set, and must be flagged as such.

findings.headline: Egypt's national carpet and floor-covering exports were USD 398.02m in 2025 (USD 106.52m to the United States) at an average 2024 export price of ~USD 14/sqm, +1.6% YoY
findings.source_name: UN COMTRADE via Trading Economics, Egypt exports of carpets and other textile floor coverings
findings.detail: MARKET DATA ONLY — external context, never an ORWE-reported figure. IT DOES NOT RECONCILE with the company's own realised price and the gap is left open rather than papered over: ORWE's FY2024 international revenue of EGP 16,049m over 70,629k sqm is EGP 227/sqm, roughly USD 4.8/sqm at a ~47.5 average rate. The national average is about three times that. The likely causes are mix (ORWE's international volume is heavily tufted and non-woven) and the fact that OW USA's American sales are not Egyptian exports at all. A build must not use the national average as an ASP benchmark without resolving this.
findings.model_impact: Context for the ASP driver only. The ASP driver itself is built from the company's own volume and value tables (F16), not from this.

findings.headline: Named entrants into Egypt's textile cluster since early 2025: Boni (Turkey, USD 100m integrated factory, 10th of Ramadan City), EVERFAR Textile Egypt LLC (China, USD 130m), Changzhou Kingcason Printing & Dyeing (China, USD 24.5m) and Shanghai Honour Home Textile. Egypt's textile market is otherwise highly fragmented — 14,000+ companies, with state-owned enterprises holding ~40-45% of spinning and weaving capacity
findings.source_name: Ecofin Agency; Kohan Textile Journal; Mordor Intelligence Egypt textile manufacturing study
findings.detail: Every named entrant is in garments, printing and dyeing, or home textiles. NONE is a machine-woven carpet line. The distinction is preserved rather than blurred; see also F42.
findings.model_impact: Sets the domestic competitive-pressure term. Management's own language for the Egypt leg in 1Q- and 2Q-2026 is 'intensifying competition' alongside a 15% YoY woven volume decline in 2Q-2026, so the domestic volume driver is modelled DOWN with price up — not both up.

findings.headline: Luxury vinyl tile is the substitution threat and it is growing fast: the LVT market goes from ~USD 29.4bn in 2025 to ~USD 33.33bn in 2026, +13.4%, driven by renovation demand replacing ageing carpet in North America and Europe and by carpet-tile replacement in high-traffic commercial areas. Carpets and rugs have lost share to hard surfaces for a decade and are expected to keep doing so — BUT area rugs have been relatively unaffected, because they are laid over hard-surface flooring
findings.source_name: The Business Research Company LVT market report 2026; Mordor Intelligence LVT floor covering market; Freedonia global carpets and rugs coverage
findings.model_impact: Asymmetric, and the asymmetry is the whole point for this issuer. ORWE's revenue is 77-78% WOVEN, i.e. area rugs, which the substitution literature explicitly exempts, and only ~11-12% tufted wall-to-wall in Egypt, which it does not. Sets the TERMINAL growth rate: low single-digit real, with the wall-to-wall tufted leg gliding below the woven leg rather than one blended decline rate for the whole company.

findings.headline: Named competitor actions: Mohawk Industries took pricing actions and productivity and restructuring gains through 2Q-2026, guided 3Q-2026 adjusted EPS to USD 2.50-2.60 including ~USD 0.12 of tariff refunds, and warned of higher input costs into 4Q-2026 with a 'potential need for additional pricing actions'. Merinos Hali (Erdemoglu Holding) is the largest machine-made carpet producer in Turkey, anchoring the Gaziantep cluster alongside Artemis and Atlas; Victoria PLC owns the former Balta rug and carpet division
findings.source_name: Mohawk Industries 2Q-2026 results release and earnings call, 30-Jul-2026; Kohan Textile Journal and Pelotek on the Turkish machine-made carpet cluster
findings.detail: Mohawk signalling further price rises into 4Q-2026 on input cost is the same polypropylene shock ORWE reports (F02, F21), which means the cost push is industry-wide and therefore more likely to be passed through than absorbed.
findings.model_impact: Supports modelling ASP UP through 2H-2026 in both Egypt and export markets rather than assuming ORWE absorbs the PP move, and constrains how far margin may be assumed to expand: the whole industry is repricing, so this is cost pass-through, not share gain.

At 30-6-2026: banks-credit accounts 7,666,411,514 + long-term loans 59,655,102 + long-term current portion 104,859,923 = gross debt 7,830,926,539; lease liabilities 406,973,814 + 186,158,386 = 593,132,200; cash 6,868,306,946 + treasury bills 1,609,554,830 + financial assets at amortised cost 1,062,487,721 = 9,540,349,497. findings.detail: THE DEFINITION IS THEREFORE KNOWN AND REPRODUCIBLE: net debt = bank facilities + loans + LEASE LIABILITIES - cash - treasury bills - financial assets at amortised cost. Prior points on the company's own series: net debt EGP 2,044m at 31-12-2022, EGP 121m at 31-12-2023, EGP 1.8bn at 31-12-2024 (0.5x EBITDA), EGP 0.6bn at 31-12-2025 (0.2x), net CASH EGP 1.2bn at 31-3-2026 and EGP 1.1bn at 30-6-2026. See F27 and F40.
findings.model_impact: Sets the EV-to-equity bridge, in which net cash ADDS, and confirms the balance sheet is not a constraint on the forecast. Use the company's own definition or state the departure.

Audited other revenues: FY2023 329,050,807; FY2024 594,252,959; FY2025 454,183,569; Q1-2026 201,359,682; Q2-2026 452,201,877; H1-2026 653,561,559. FY2025's EGP 454m splits as EGP 254m current programme plus EGP 200m backlog claims, with EGP 180m of backlog remaining; 2Q-2026's EGP 452m includes EGP 150m of backlog settled through government fee offsets. Export-rebate income becomes a bottom-up build — current accrual on export value plus a dated run-off of the named EGP 180m backlog — instead of a plug inside 'other income'. It must also be shown SEPARATELY in the earnings bridge: a third of half-year profit is a government programme, not operations.

findings.headline: Treasury and interest income are separately disclosed and tie to management's figure: FY2025 treasury-bill returns 430,930,850 + financial assets at amortised cost returns 131,952,040 + interest income 253,316,404 = 816,199,294, against the FY2025 release's 'Interest Income was EGP 817m'. findings.detail: ORWE earns MORE on its cash than it pays on its debt: EGP 816m of investment income against EGP 536m of finance cost in FY2025. The treasury book — treasury bills EGP 805m, financial assets at amortised cost EGP 492m and cash EGP 4,633m at 31-12-2025 — is EGP-denominated and earning Egyptian policy-rate yields while the debt is foreign-currency (F27). findings.model_impact: Treasury income is a bottom-up yield on the modelled cash and treasury-bill balance at the CBE path, not a growth rate. Exclude it from FCFF and handle it in the equity bridge so the cash is not counted twice.

findings.model_impact: THE DRIVER UNLOCK OF THE WHOLE BUILD. Converts revenue from a growth rate into six independent volume-times-ASP legs: woven, tufted and non-woven, each split Egypt and international. GAP FLAGGED: this level of disclosure exists ONLY for FY2023 and FY2024. From FY2025 the company publishes segment MIX percentages and YoY volume and ASP CHANGES, not levels, so FY2025 and FY2026 legs must be rolled forward off the FY2024 base and reconciled back to audited revenue, with the reconciliation shown.

findings.headline: FY2022 and FY2021 net sales by volume and value: woven Egypt-based EGP 8,367.1m / 6,685.5m on 61.03 / 62.47m sqm; OW USA EGP 2,165.5m / 1,949.6m on 11.85 / 14.44m sqm; OW China EGP 1.2m / 22.3m on 0.01 / 0.23m sqm; tufted EGP 2,057.2m / 2,138.2m on 32.21 / 41.72m sqm; non-woven felt EGP 555.3m / 522.3m on 16.71 / 19.88m sqm; other EGP 109.4m / 85.5m. Group total EGP 13,255.7m / 11,403.4m on 121.8 / 138.7m sqm
findings.source_name: ORWE 4Q-2022 Earnings Release, 27-Feb-2023, Tables 1 and 2
findings.detail: The value total of 13,255.7 ties to the audited FY2022 net sales of 13,255,653,997. THE CURRENCY POINT, IN THE COMPANY'S OWN NUMBERS: from FY2022 to FY2025 EGP revenue rose 100.8% (13,255.7 to 26,622.8) while VOLUME FELL 8.7% (121.8 to 111.2m sqm). The entire top line is price, and management attributes that price to devaluation in almost every period — 'ASP was up 12% YoY ... driven by devaluation', '36% YoY higher ASP due to currency devaluation'. Also note the China facility is effectively gone at 0.01m sqm in FY2022, and a disclosure of the sale of the China plant sits on the company's disclosure page dated 10-Aug-2022.
findings.model_impact: Sets the volume base and proves the growth decomposition the model must carry: volume and price forecast SEPARATELY and in both directions, with the price leg split between currency translation and real pricing. A single revenue growth rate would hide a four-year volume decline.

findings.headline: FY2025 results release, 26-Feb-2026, published 01-Mar-2026: revenue EGP 26.6bn +10%, gross profit EGP 3.4bn +8% at 12.6%, EBITDA EGP 3.6bn +2% at 13.4%, adjusted net attributable profit EGP 2.3bn +5.4%. International 67% of revenue and 63% of volume (EGP 17.9bn), Egypt 33% and 37% (EGP 8.7bn). International: woven volume +5% ASP +12% revenue +17%; tufted volume -9% ASP +5% revenue -5%; non-woven volume +2% ASP +6% revenue +8%. Egypt: woven volume -6% ASP +13%; tufted volume -12% ASP +12%; non-woven volume +4% ASP +5%. Claims 100bp of global market-share gain
findings.source_name: ORWE FY-2025 Earnings Release
findings.detail: EBITDA DEFINITION SOLVED AND REPRODUCIBLE: gross profit minus distribution minus G&A plus fixed-asset depreciation plus right-of-use depreciation. FY2025: 3,350,262,617 - 299,019,544 - 752,483,532 + 1,117,728,751 + 159,152,334 = 3,575,640,626, the stated EGP 3,576m. FY2024: 3,103,175,922 - 254,754,592 - 630,066,477 + 1,159,905,573 + 135,886,499 = 3,514,146,925, the stated 3,514m. It EXCLUDES other revenues, treasury income, expected credit loss and provisions. TWO ERRORS IN THIS RELEASE'S OWN CHARTS, recorded rather than repeated: the FY2025 COGS bar reads 6.1, which is the 4Q figure while the text says EGP 23bn, and the FY2025 G&A bar reads 287 while the text says EGP 752m. Its balance-sheet summary is also on a different basis from the audited statements — see F34.
findings.model_impact: Fixes the EBITDA bridge so the study reconciles to the company's published measure rather than inventing a third definition, and supplies the FY2025 volume and ASP CHANGES needed to roll the FY2024 segment matrix forward.

findings.headline: 2Q-2026 results release, 11-Aug-2026 — the newest operating anchor on the record, and the one that supersedes everything older. Revenue EGP 7.0bn +13% YoY, EBITDA EGP 0.9bn +18% at 13.5%, net profit EGP 1.1bn +98% at 16.1%, free cash flow EGP 0.3bn, cash conversion cycle 169 days (-10 days), net debt to EBITDA -0.3x, ROIC 30.4%. INTERNATIONAL 70% OF REVENUE AND 67% OF VOLUME (EGP 4.9bn); EGYPT 30% AND 33% (EGP 2.1bn). International woven revenue +22% on volume +20% and ASP +2% 'due to currency depreciation'; tufted export revenue +5% on volume +5%; non-woven export revenue -13% on volume -23% with ASP +13%. Egypt woven revenue +7% despite volume -15%, on ASP +25%; Egypt tufted volume -3% ASP +3%; Egypt non-woven ASP +12% drove volume -17%. Destination mix: Americas 34%, Europe 25%, Egypt 30%, GCC 4%, Africa 4%, Asia 2%, hospitality and others 1%. Egypt channel mix: wholesale 45%, showrooms 40%, depots 11%, hospitality 5%, e-commerce under 1%. Capex EGP 364m, 5% of sales, with full-year capex guided to EGP 1.2bn
findings.source_name: ORWE 2Q-2026 Earnings Release
findings.detail: A NEWER RELEASE'S ANCHORS SUPERSEDE OLDER ONES [L-008 / MODON]. Export share is 70% of revenue at 2Q-2026, not the 67% of FY2025 or the 66% of FY2024, and the destination mix is Americas 34% / Europe 25%, not the FY2025 deck's 29% / 24%. Any driver still carrying the FY2025 figures is stale by one reporting cycle. COGS EGP 6.0bn +10% YoY on manufacturing overheads +15% and labour +21% with raw materials +4%; G&A EGP 283m, +55%.

findings.headline: Quarterly VOLUME series in millions of square metres with the international/Egypt split, from the investor presentations: 4Q-2024 31.2 (68/32), 1Q-2025 27.2 (60/40), 2Q-2025 25.5 (62/38), 3Q-2025 27.2 (67/33), 4Q-2025 31.3 (63/37); restated in the 2Q-2026 deck as 2Q-2025 25.5, 3Q-2025 27.1, 4Q-2025 31.1, 1Q-2026 29.4 (63/37), 2Q-2026 25.6 (67/33). 4Q-2025 volume mix woven 56%, tufted 26%, non-woven 18% against a revenue mix of woven 77%, tufted 17%, non-woven 6%; 2Q-2026 volume mix woven 59%, tufted 27%, non-woven 14%
findings.source_name: ORWE 4Q-2025 Investor Presentation, 01-Mar-2026, page 2, and 2Q-2026 Investor Presentation, 11-Aug-2026, page 4, both read off the rendered pixels
findings.detail: FY2025 volume = 27.2 + 25.5 + 27.2 + 31.3 = 111.2m sqm, which over the audited 26,622,797,999 gives a group realised price of EGP 239.4/sqm. TWO DEFECTS FLAGGED. (1) The 2Q-2026 deck restates 3Q-2025 from 27.2 to 27.1 and 4Q-2025 from 31.3 to 31.1, moving FY2025 volume to 111.0m sqm. (2) The 2Q-2026 revenue-mix donut prints woven 78% / tufted 17% / non-woven 22%, which sums to 117 — a printing error in the deck, not a reading error; prefer the 2Q-2026 release's own segment split.

findings.headline: THE COMPANY'S OWN POLYPROPYLENE SERIES. From the 2Q-2026 deck: a quarterly polypropylene figure of 989 (2Q-2025), 952 (3Q-2025), 892 (4Q-2025), 948 (1Q-2026) and 1,246 (2Q-2026), with polypropylene as a share of raw materials of 52.0%, 49.0%, 47.0%, 51.0% and 51.0%. Raw materials 2Q-2026 EGP 3.1bn split polypropylene/nylon 51%, backing 21%, finishing material 20%, wool 7%, with YoY changes of +3%, -3%, +8% and +30%. From the 4Q-2025 deck: COGS EGP 6.2bn split raw materials 50%, others 21%, selling expenses 16%, wages 10%, depreciation 3%, with raw materials EGP 3.1bn split polypropylene/nylon 47%, backing 24%, finishing 22%, wool 7%, and COGS component YoY of raw materials -6%, wages +25%, depreciation -19%, selling -8%, others +32%
findings.source_name: ORWE 2Q-2026 Investor Presentation page 6 and 4Q-2025 Investor Presentation page 4, both read off the rendered pixels
findings.detail: INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY, FLAGGED NOT RECONCILED: the polypropylene bar chart is captioned '(EGP B)' but the values are plainly EGP millions, and 1,246 at a stated 51% of raw materials implies raw materials of EGP 2,443m, not the EGP 3.1bn the donut on the same page states. The two disclosures on one slide do not tie. A build must pick one basis, state which, and sensitise the other. The polypropylene series is itself internally coherent and moves +31% q/q into 2Q-2026, matching the external polymer repricing in F02.
findings.model_impact: DRIVER UNLOCK for cost per unit. Raw-material cost per square metre = polypropylene spend divided by its share of raw materials divided by volume, escalated on the polypropylene price path, with SEPARATE escalators for wages (+21% to +27% YoY) and for overheads [L-009: one escalator per cost driver, never one blended rate].

findings.headline: Management guidance on the record: FY2026 capex of EGP 1.2bn, stated identically in the 1Q-2026 release of 20-May-2026 ('focused on capacity expansion, overhauling, and digital transformation') and the 2Q-2026 release of 11-Aug-2026 ('feeding lines, production capacity, H&S and digital transformation'). Actual capex was EGP 453m in FY2023, EGP 786m in FY2024 and EGP 974m in FY2025
findings.source_name: ORWE 1Q-2026 and 2Q-2026 Earnings Releases
findings.detail: CONTRADICTION BETWEEN THE COMPANY'S OWN RELEASES, RECORDED: the 1Q-2026 release states Q1 capex of EGP 150m while the 2Q-2026 release's chart puts 1Q-2026 capex at EGP 220m. The 2Q chart is internally consistent with its own text (2Q EGP 364m, +88% on 2Q-2025's 193m and +65% on 220m), so 220m is the more likely figure — but the disagreement is left visible. Against EGP 1.2bn of guidance, half-year actuals of either 514m or 584m imply a large second-half step-up. Per [L-012] guidance is SCORED against outcome, never used as a model input.
findings.model_impact: Capex is built from the audited cash-flow history and the disclosed capacity position, with the EGP 1.2bn guidance carried as a scored management target in the guidance-tracking table rather than as the driver.

findings.headline: The Extraordinary General Assembly of 13-Aug-2025 widened the company's stated objective to include production of all types of woven and non-woven textiles and furnishings, READY-MADE GARMENTS, all kinds of yarns and threads from natural, synthetic or blended materials, spinning, weaving, dyeing, printing and finishing, and the production, import, export and installation of all types of movable FURNITURE and household supplies
findings.source_name: ORWE FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements, note 1-3 'Company's objective', read off the rendered pixels, printed page 8
findings.detail: A materially broader charter than machine-woven carpets, adopted eleven months before this sweep and unaccompanied by any quantified plan, capex line or target. It is a permission, not yet a business.
findings.model_impact: Not modelled as revenue — there is nothing to model from. It IS modelled as an option on the capex path and as a reason the terminal reinvestment rate should not be set at maintenance level. Flag it in the study rather than let it surface later as a surprise.

findings.headline: BASE CHANGER. In H1-2026 Oriental Weavers subscribed to a capital increase of its subsidiary Egyptian Fibers Company (EFCO) for 26,290,753 shares of EGP 10 nominal value each, taking its holding from 69.26% to 88.12%. The subsidiary schedule moves on this line only — OW USA 82.68%, OW International 99.99%, MAC Carpet Mills 58.29%, New Mac 57.12% and OW Textile 71.44% are all unchanged
findings.source_name: ORWE 30-6-2026 reviewed consolidated financial statements, note 4 'Scope of consolidated financial statements' and its footnote, read off the rendered pixels, printed page 9
findings.detail: THE NAMED TRANSACTION, SEARCHED AS A NAMED TRANSACTION AND FOUND IN THE FILING ITSELF — it is not on the company's Reports & Disclosures page, which stops at Oct-2024. 26,290,753 x EGP 10 = EGP 262,907,530 of nominal subscription. The effect is visible in the accounts: non-controlling interest falls from 1,966,368,620 at 31-12-2025 to 1,731,842,390 at 30-6-2026 while total equity rises, and management attributes part of the 2Q-2026 net-attributable-profit jump to 'the increased ownership stake in EFCO'. EFCO is the group's polypropylene and polyester-fibre arm, i.e. the vertical integration into the input that is roughly a quarter of cost of sales.
findings.model_impact: Resets the NCI base from H1-2026 onward: an explicit dated step, dual-framed with and without, NEVER smoothed into an NCI percentage glide. It also raises the group's share of the polypropylene margin, which changes the consolidated sensitivity to the polypropylene price in F02 and F21 — the same input now hurts less at the attributable line.

findings.headline: Two further dated one-offs inside the window. First, in FY2024 management wrote down EGP 0.5bn of old finished goods 'as part of cleanup', which is the whole of the FY2024 gross-margin drop from 14.4% to 12.8% — adjusted gross margin was 15.0% and adjusted EBITDA margin 16.7%. Second, in 1Q-2026 the group booked EGP 328,495,398 of capital gains on the sale of unproductive assets in Egypt and the USA, rising to EGP 362,386,692 for H1-2026
findings.source_name: ORWE FY2024 Earnings Release, 27-Feb-2025, for the write-down; ORWE 31-3-2026 and 30-6-2026 reviewed consolidated income statements for the capital gains
findings.detail: The capital-gain figures are audited income-statement lines, not a management adjustment: 'Capital gain 328 495 398' in the Q1-2026 filing and 'Gain from sale of fixed assets 362 386 692' for H1-2026, and the company's own adjusted net profit of EGP 1.7bn for H1-2026 strips exactly EGP 0.3bn of them.
findings.model_impact: BOTH are explicit dated events, dual-framed. The FY2024 write-down is stripped when FY2024 is used as a normalisation base; the 2026 disposal gains are excluded from the forward earnings base entirely. Neither may be smoothed into a margin glide — doing so would make FY2024 look structurally worse and FY2026 structurally better than either is.

findings.headline: Shareholder structure at 30-6-2026, dated and disclosed: Khamis family 54% (of which M&M Khamis 29% and FYK 25%), Fitihi Group 12%, Ataqa Group 6%, Olayan Holding 3%, local institutions 12%, foreign institutions 7%, local retail 4%, foreign retail 2%. At 31-12-2025 the same table read Khamis 54.1% (FKY 24.6%), Fitihi 11.8%, Ataqa 5%, Olayan 3%, local institutions 11%, foreign institutions 4%, local retail 8%, foreign retail 2%
findings.source_name: ORWE 2Q-2026 Earnings Release, 'Shareholders' Structure - YoY, As of 30-6-2026'; ORWE FY-2025 Earnings Release, 'As of 31-12-2025'
findings.detail: NAMED-TRANSACTION RULE APPLIED: no named change-of-control or block transaction was found for the Khamis, Fitihi, Ataqa or Olayan holdings — see the dated negative search F41. The movement between the two dates (foreign institutions 4% to 7%, local retail 8% to 4%) is a free-float rotation with no announced trade behind it, and is recorded as such rather than as an 'estimated' stake change. The company's own Stock Overview page carries a DIFFERENT, undated and rounded split — foreign institutions 19%, local institutions 20%, retail 7% — so use the dated release.
findings.model_impact: Fixes the free float at roughly 46% and confirms a stable controlling family block, which is an input to the liquidity and control discussion, not to cash flow. The only ownership event that touches a number is the EFCO subscription in F24.

findings.headline: Share count and capital: 665,107,268 listed common shares at EGP 1 par, issued and paid-in capital EGP 665,107,268 against authorised capital of EGP 1,000,000,000, listed on the Egyptian Exchange since 25-Aug-1993. The share count is unchanged across all four audited years and both 2026 interims. Dividends per the company's own table: FY2025 EGP 1.50 (paid from 20-May-2026), FY2023 EGP 1.25 (30-Apr-2024), FY2022 EGP 0.60 (17-May-2023), FY2021 EGP 1.00 (18-Apr-2022)
findings.source_name: ORWE Stock Overview corporate-information block and Result Center dividends table; share capital confirmed in the audited balance sheets and note 19
findings.detail: TWO THINGS A BUILD WOULD GET WRONG. (1) THE EPS PRINTED IN THE CONSOLIDATED STATEMENTS IS NOT CONSOLIDATED EPS. Note 30 derives it from the SEPARATE company's profit: FY2025 2,125,780,942 less employees' share 110,851,211 less board remuneration 3,200,000 = 2,011,729,731 over 665,107,268 shares = EGP 3.02. Consolidated attributable EPS is 2,189,343,558 / 665,107,268 = EGP 3.29. The H1-2026 filing prints 2.79 for the half and 0.21 for the quarter, which cannot both be the same measure. (2) THE DIVIDEND TABLE HAS NO FY2024 ROW AND DOES NOT RECONCILE to the statement of changes in equity, which charges parent dividends of 1,102,870,691 in FY2024 (EGP 1.66 a share) and 1,412,063,405 in FY2025 (EGP 2.12 a share) against table entries of EGP 1.25 and EGP 1.50. The gap is not explained in any document read here.
findings.model_impact: Sets the share count for every per-share figure and forces the study to compute its own consolidated EPS rather than lift note 30. The dividend driver is built off the SOCIE charge, with the table shown beside it and the difference disclosed.

findings.headline: THE CURRENCY POSITION, ASSEMBLED FROM THE COMPANY'S OWN DISCLOSURES. (a) Dollar-linked revenue: the 4Q-2023 release states SG&A fell as a share of sales because expenses are 'EGP-denominated ... in contrast to the 59% USD-based revenues'; international revenue has since risen to 67% in FY2025 and 70% in 2Q-2026. (b) Dollar-linked debt: the FY2024 release states total debt of EGP 7.4bn, +59% YoY, was '99% foreign, 1% local', with the rise attributed to devaluation. (c) The translation reserve in equity: 3,541,296,155 (2021), 6,258,366,013 (2022), 7,904,577,917 (2023), 12,810,841,902 (2024), 11,995,255,064 (2025), 13,893,397,475 (31-3-2026), 12,276,104,950 (30-6-2026). (d) The income statement's foreign-exchange line: FY2022 (72,646,826), FY2023 (166,163,055), FY2024 (351,533,473), FY2025 (51,440,512), H1-2026 (60,242,121)
findings.source_name: ORWE audited consolidated statements FY2022-FY2025 and the 2026 interims — balance sheets, income statements and statements of changes in equity — cross-read with the 4Q-2023 and FY2024 earnings releases
findings.detail: THE POINT A MARGIN READ WOULD MISS. The currency effect is overwhelmingly in OCI, not in profit. The translation reserve moved +EGP 1,898m in 1Q-2026 and -EGP 1,617m in 2Q-2026 — each larger, in one quarter, than that quarter's entire net profit of EGP 893m and EGP 1,121m — while the income statement's FX line was only (74.9m) and +14.7m. Meanwhile the FINANCE COST is dollar-priced: FY2025 bank interest of 472,721,255 over average bank facilities of 6,781,342,800 is an implied 6.97% against a 19-20% EGP policy rate. A build that charges an EGP cost of debt on this balance sheet overstates finance cost roughly threefold.
findings.model_impact: Makes FX a DRIVER, not a footnote, in four separate places: the ASP path on 70% of revenue; the cost of the imported polypropylene that is a quarter of COGS; the cost of debt, which is dollar-priced and must NOT take the CBE rate; and the OCI translation reserve, which must be forecast separately from profit and must not leak into the earnings base. OPEN GAP: no quantified foreign-currency asset and liability table, no FX sensitivity and no hedging disclosure exists anywhere in the filings — see the negative search F40.

findings.headline: LISTING AND PRICE SERIES, RECORDED; NO BETA RESOLVED. ORWE is listed on the Egyptian Exchange only — note 1-5 of the FY2025 statements says simply 'The Company is listed in Egyptian exchange', and the Stock Overview page gives a single listing dated 25-Aug-1993 with 665,107,268 listed shares. The local price series is engine/raw_ohlc/EG/ORWE.csv: 3,749 daily rows from 03-Jan-2011 at EGP 4.53 to 23-Aug-2026 at EGP 26.00, quoted in Egyptian pounds. The matching exchange index is engine/raw_indices/EG/EGX30.csv, running to 08-Sep-2026 at 56,174.30
findings.source_name: ORWE FY2025 audited consolidated financial statements note 1-5; orientalweavers.com Stock Overview; local repository series
findings.detail: DUAL-LISTING TRAP CHECKED AND CLEARED — see the dated negative search F43. No GDR, ADR or second exchange line was found, so the Orascom Construction problem of two legitimate regressors for one issuer does not arise here: one series, one index. MAGNITUDE CHECK: 665,107,268 shares at EGP 26.00 is a market capitalisation of EGP 17.29bn against attributable book equity of EGP 20.04bn at 30-6-2026, a price-to-book of 0.86 — a plausible EGX magnitude, so the series is in pounds and not piastres. STALENESS: the ORWE file's last row is 23-Aug-2026, seventeen days before this sweep, while the index runs to 08-Sep-2026. NO BETA WAS RESOLVED, BY INSTRUCTION; when one is needed it must come from engine/beta_regression.py:own_stock_beta('ORWE', 'EG', 'EGX'), never from a study-local script.

findings.headline: A Q1-2026 RESTATEMENT FOUND BY RE-ADDING, NOT BY READING. Q1-2026 as filed plus Q2-2026 as filed does not equal H1-2026 as filed: cost of sales 6,086,688,840 + 5,968,410,585 = 12,055,099,425 against the printed H1 figure of 12,089,440,761, a gap of EGP 34,341,336, with gross profit out by the same amount the other way. The offset is exactly traceable: 'formed provisions and impairment' is 34,543,447 in the Q1 filing and 20,203,314 in the Q2 column, summing to 54,746,761 against the printed H1 figure of 20,405,425 — a difference of EGP 34,341,336, the same number. Net profit is unaffected: 893,001,434 + 1,121,416,247 = 2,014,417,681 exactly
findings.source_name: ORWE 31-3-2026 and 30-6-2026 reviewed consolidated income statements, re-added against each other
findings.detail: EGP 34,341,336 was reclassified out of provisions and into cost of sales between the two filings. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MARGIN PATH: Q1-2026 gross profit on the H1 basis is 858,122,604 - 34,341,336 = 823,781,268, a gross margin of 11.86% rather than the 12.36% in the Q1 filing and the 12.4% quoted in both the 1Q-2026 and 2Q-2026 releases. A quarterly margin path taken from the releases is 50bp too high in Q1-2026 and will make the first-to-second-quarter improvement look smaller than it was.
findings.model_impact: Forces the quarterly margin series onto ONE consistent basis — the H1 filing's — and the basis to be stated. Touches the gross-margin OUTPUT and the 2026 seasonality shape directly.

findings.headline: COLUMN AND ROW LABELS IN THE FILINGS AND RELEASES THAT ARE WRONG, each found by arithmetic. (1) The 30-6-2026 income statement's fourth column is headed 'From 1/1/2025 To 30/6/2025' but carries EGP 6,167,512,621 of net sales — the Q2-2025 quarter, not the half; the half is the second column at 12,565,352,630. (2) The 1Q-2026 release's balance-sheet summary columns headed '1Q 25' and '1Q 26' hold 31-Dec-2025 and 31-Mar-2026 positions, and its cash-flow summary's lower rows are FY2024 and FY2025 full-year figures under the same quarterly headings. (3) The 2Q-2026 release's balance-sheet column headed '1H 2025' holds 31-Dec-2025 figures — inventory 10,153 is the audited 10,152,672,252. (4) The FY2025 release's COGS and G&A charts print the fourth-quarter figure and a wrong number respectively in the FY2025 slot
findings.source_name: ORWE 30-6-2026 reviewed consolidated income statement; the 1Q-2026, 2Q-2026 and FY-2025 earnings releases, each tied back to the audited statements
findings.detail: None of these is a reading error; each was confirmed by matching the printed value to a figure that is unambiguous elsewhere. THE ARITHMETIC IS THE ARBITER, NOT THE LABEL. Also recorded: the FY2025 statement of changes in equity opens FY2024 with net profit of EGP 1,740,203,594 while the FY2023 and FY2024 statements print 1,740,203,598 — an EGP 4 difference, re-rendered at 300 dpi and re-read to rule out a glyph misread. Each filing foots internally, so it is presentation, not restatement.
findings.model_impact: Protects every historical series in the model from a mislabelled lift. Any quarterly or half-yearly figure taken from a release must be tied back to the filing before it enters a driver.

findings.headline: THE EARNINGS RELEASES' BALANCE-SHEET SUMMARIES ARE ON A DIFFERENT BASIS FROM THE AUDITED STATEMENTS AND MUST NOT BE USED. The FY2025 release prints FY2025 total assets of EGP 33,745m, inventory 10,581m, fixed assets 7,752m and equity 20,375m; the audited statements print 33,078.567m, 10,152.672m, 8,145.992m and 20,832.202m. For FY2024 the release prints total assets of 32,896m against an audited 34,904.567m
findings.source_name: ORWE FY-2025 Earnings Release balance-sheet summary compared with the FY2025 audited consolidated statement of financial position
findings.detail: The differences are large — 6% on FY2024 total assets — and no reconciliation is given anywhere. By contrast the SAME release's income-statement and cash-flow summaries tie to the audited statements exactly: revenue 24,289 and 26,623, net profit 2,542 and 2,263, operating cash flow 1,910 and 3,191, closing cash 4,233 and 4,844. So the release is reliable on profit and cash flow and unreliable on the balance sheet.
findings.model_impact: Every balance-sheet driver — working capital, net debt, invested capital, the equity bridge — is built from the AUDITED statements only. The release's balance-sheet table is excluded from the model and the exclusion is stated.

findings.headline: Negative search — nothing found (searched: ORWE FY2025 audited consolidated statements note 34 'Financial instruments and risk management' in full, plus notes 26 and 29, plus the 30-6-2026 interim notes, for a quantified foreign-currency asset and liability table, an FX sensitivity analysis, a hedging or forward-contract policy, and the average and closing EGP/USD rates used for translation. NOTHING IS DISCLOSED. Note 34's exchange-rate-risk paragraph reads in full: 'This risk is considered acceptable because of the assets in foreign currency correspond to the company's obligations in foreign currencies' — no figures, no sensitivity, no hedge. Note 26 gives the EGP 6,613,356,814 of bank facilities as a single number with no currency split and no interest rate; the only currency split ever published is the FY2024 release's '99% foreign, 1% local'. Also searched for a dated annual-average EGP/USD series from a primary source: cbe.org.eg was WAF-blocked, support ID da44b8f3-d541-4d41-af65-ffc44ffcdaa2, and none was obtained)

NO named block trade, tender offer, change of control or announced disposal was found for the Khamis, Fitihi Group, Ataqa Group or Olayan Holding stakes in 2025 or 2026, and NO EGX disclosure of the EFCO subscription exists on the company's own disclosure page — that page's newest item is dated 21-Oct-2024. The EFCO transaction in F24 was found inside the 30-6-2026 interim statements themselves. The latest tender-offer-related item on the record is the 21-Oct-2024 disclosure that there is NO offer for the company's shares)

drivers.driver: Sales volume (m sqm) by product segment x geography — woven / tufted / non-woven, Egypt / international
drivers.justification: Built off the FY2023-FY2024 volume matrix in thousands of square metres, which ties to the audited top line to the pound, rolled forward on the disclosed quarterly volume series (25.5 to 31.3m sqm a quarter) and the per-segment YoY volume changes in each release, and capped by the disclosed nameplate of 150m sqm (woven 79 / tufted 48.1 / non-woven 23). GAP FLAGGED: segment-by-geography LEVELS are disclosed only for FY2023 and FY2024; FY2025-26 legs are rolled off that base and must be reconciled back to audited revenue, with the reconciliation shown.

drivers.driver: Realised price per sqm (ASP), same six legs, split into currency translation and real pricing
drivers.justification: Solved as revenue over volume on each leg from the same disclosed matrix — group EGP 108.8/sqm in FY2022, 156.7 in FY2023, 213.5 in FY2024, 239.4 in FY2025 — then projected on the per-leg ASP changes the company publishes every quarter, each of which management attributes explicitly either to devaluation or to a pricing action. Volume and price are projected SEPARATELY and in both directions, because EGP revenue doubled from FY2022 to FY2025 while volume fell 8.7%.

drivers.driver: International (export) share of revenue and volume, and destination mix
drivers.justification: Disclosed directly and dated, with the newest disclosure superseding: 70% of revenue and 67% of volume at 2Q-2026, against 67% and 63% for FY2025 and 66% and 62% for FY2024. Destination mix at 2Q-2026 is Americas 34%, Europe 25%, Egypt 30%, GCC 4%, Africa 4%, Asia 2%, hospitality and others 1%. Carried at the newest figures, not the FY2025 ones.

drivers.driver: EGP/USD path — applied to the export ASP leg, the imported polypropylene leg, the dollar-priced debt leg and the OCI translation reserve
drivers.justification: TOP-DOWN OF NECESSITY, AND SAID SO. The company discloses no FX sensitivity, no quantified foreign-currency position, no hedging policy and no translation rates — note 34 says only that the risk is 'acceptable' — and the CBE's own site was WAF-blocked, so no primary average-rate series was obtained either. The path is therefore set exogenously from the market rate (~51.0 EGP/USD on 09-Sep-2026, -6.4% year to date) and the CBE's own published inflation target, and it is SENSITISED as the single largest swing factor in the study.

drivers.driver: Raw-material cost per sqm — polypropylene / nylon leg
drivers.justification: The company publishes a quarterly polypropylene figure (989 / 952 / 892 / 948 / 1,246 from 2Q-2025 to 2Q-2026), polypropylene as a share of raw materials (52% / 49% / 47% / 51% / 51%), raw materials as a share of COGS (50% at 4Q-2025) and volume — which together are enough to build a cost per square metre. GAP FLAGGED: the polypropylene bar and the EGP 3.1bn raw-material donut on the same slide do not reconcile (1,246 at 51% implies EGP 2,443m, not 3,100m); the build states which basis it uses and sensitises the other. Corroborated externally by the +27% to +32% polymer repricing of 1Q-2026.

drivers.driver: Backing, finishing material and wool cost per sqm
drivers.justification: Disclosed as shares of raw materials with their own YoY changes — backing 21% (-3%), finishing 20% (+8%), wool 7% (+30%) at 2Q-2026, against 24% / 22% / 7% at 4Q-2025. Each gets its OWN escalator; wool at +30% and backing at -3% are not the same input and are not escalated together [L-009].

Wages are a disclosed 10% of COGS with a disclosed YoY change every quarter — +25% in 4Q-2025, +27% in 1Q-2026, +21% in 2Q-2026 — so the leg is built on the disclosed base and its own escalator rather than a blended inflation rate. The mechanism is named and external: competition for skilled labour in the same 10th of Ramadan cluster the Turkish and Chinese entrants are building into.

The 21% 'Others' bucket of COGS is NOT decomposed anywhere, and neither the company nor any obtainable source gives the industrial energy-tariff path at plant level or a pass-through mechanism. Built as a rate on the volume base escalated on the disclosed aggregate change (+15% YoY at 2Q-2026, +11% at 1Q-2026) and sensitised. The coarser level is used because the disclosure stops there, and that is said rather than hidden.

drivers.driver: Gross margin — OUTPUT, never an input
drivers.justification: NOT SET. Revenue is the sum of six volume-times-ASP legs and cost of sales is the sum of the raw-material, labour and overhead legs above; the margin is whatever falls out, and is then checked against the filed series — 9.48% FY2022, 14.44% FY2023, 12.78% FY2024, 12.58% FY2025, 11.86% Q1-2026 on the H1 basis, 14.20% Q2-2026. Setting a contribution or gross margin as an input here would be a QC FAIL, because the filings disclose enough to build cost per unit instead [L-005].

It IS the audited 'Other revenues' line, matched to the pound across FY2023, FY2024, FY2025, Q1-2026 and Q2-2026, so it is built as a current-programme accrual on export value plus a dated run-off of the named EGP 180m residual backlog, against the national programme's published EGP 45bn and EGP 48bn budgets and its four-year cash-plus-set-off arrears schedule. Shown SEPARATELY in the earnings bridge: it is 32% of H1-2026 net profit and it is a government programme, not operations.

Both are audited income-statement lines with quarterly levels published beside them — G&A EGP 208m in 4Q-2025, 227m in 1Q-2026 and 283m in 2Q-2026, +55% YoY — so they are built on the disclosed levels and their own growth, not as a percentage-of-sales plug.

Capex is the audited cash-flow line — EGP 453m FY2023, 786m FY2024, 974m FY2025 — against the disclosed 150m sqm nameplate at 74% utilisation; depreciation is the audited charge of EGP 1,117.7m plus EGP 159.2m of right-of-use in FY2025. The EGP 1.2bn FY2026 guidance is SCORED in the guidance table, not used as the driver [L-012], and the 150m-versus-220m contradiction between the two 2026 releases is carried openly.

drivers.driver: Cost of debt and finance expense
drivers.justification: Implied from the filings: FY2025 bank interest of EGP 472,721,255 over average bank facilities of EGP 6,781,342,800 is 6.97%, plus EGP 62,805,552 of lease interest on the disclosed lease liabilities. That rate belongs to a debt stack the company itself describes as 99% foreign currency. THE CBE'S 19-20% EGP POLICY RATE IS NOT THIS COMPANY'S COST OF DEBT, and a build that uses it overstates finance cost roughly threefold.

Three separately disclosed audited lines summing to EGP 816.2m in FY2025 against the release's stated EGP 817m, earned on a disclosed EGP-denominated book of cash, treasury bills and financial assets at amortised cost. Modelled as a yield on the modelled balance at the CBE path, excluded from FCFF and handled in the equity bridge so the cash is not counted twice.

Built from the named free-zone exemptions in note 33 — Oriental Weavers International, Oriental Weavers Textile and New Mac are exempt for life under Law No. 8 of 1997 — against the filed effective rates of 17.4% FY2022, 9.3% FY2023, 9.4% FY2024, 14.2% FY2025 and 15.2% H1-2026. Never the 22.5% statutory plug.

Built from the disclosed subsidiary ownership schedule, with the EFCO step from 69.26% to 88.12% modelled as an explicit dated event from H1-2026 and dual-framed, never smoothed into an NCI percentage glide. The NCI balance itself is the audited line: EGP 1,966,368,620 at 31-12-2025 falling to EGP 1,731,842,390 at 30-6-2026.

Built from the parent dividend charged in the audited statement of changes in equity — EGP 1,102,870,691 in FY2024 and EGP 1,412,063,405 in FY2025 — rather than from the company's own dividends table, which has no FY2024 row and does not reconcile to those charges. The declared FY2025 dividend of EGP 1.50 a share in three instalments is carried beside it and the difference is disclosed.

drivers.driver: Terminal volume growth and the long-run substitution drag
drivers.justification: No company long-range plan, volume target or capacity roadmap exists — the newest nameplate is FY2022-vintage, there is no 2026 call material of any kind, and the only forward number management publishes is one year of capex. The terminal is therefore set exogenously at low single-digit real growth, with the wall-to-wall tufted leg gliding below the woven leg because the substitution literature exempts area rugs and does not exempt wall-to-wall.

drivers.driver: OCI foreign-currency translation reserve, forecast separately from profit
drivers.justification: Cannot be built bottom-up: the company discloses no foreign-currency position, no translation rates and no sensitivity. It moved +EGP 1,898m in 1Q-2026 and -EGP 1,617m in 2Q-2026, each larger than that quarter's entire net profit, so it cannot be ignored either. Projected off the same exogenous EGP/USD path as the ASP and debt legs, kept OUT of the earnings base, and sensitised.
